findings.title: Materials' 54-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.93x forward versus 36.30x trailing, a 54-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. The market is pricing a 114 percent earnings surge that would be the steepest in the S&P 500, an aggressive bet for a sector at the 34th percentile of its own history.

findings.title: Staples' cheap forward hides rich trailing reality
findings.body: Consumer Staples sits at the 21st percentile on forward earnings but the 80th on trailing, a 60-point divergence. That gap implies analysts expect 43 percent profit growth, which would be a sharp reversal for a defensive sector whose trailing multiple is still historically elevated.

findings.title: Tech's forward percentile collapse outpaces multiple drop
findings.body: Information Technology's forward percentile fell 14 points in a month to the 11th, yet its forward P/E of 21.61 is only modestly below the market's 19.99. The percentile slide reflects a sector-wide de-rating, but the absolute multiple still demands 69 percent earnings growth — a disconnect between relative and absolute valuation.
